memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Abraham left everything he owned to Isaac. But while he was still living, he gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east." - Gen 25:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham makes a clear decision: everything he owns goes to Isaac, the son of promise. The other sons are given gifts and sent away. This was not cruelty; it was Abraham protecting the covenant line God had chosen. Isaac was the child through whom God's promises would travel forward toward Christ (Gal 3:16).

There is a gospel picture hidden here. Isaac, the promised son, receives the full inheritance. In a far greater way, everything belongs to Jesus, the true Son (Heb 1:2) — and the wonder of grace is that those who belong to Him become "heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ" (Rom 8:17). We inherit not because we earned it, but because we are joined to the Son.

Abraham also acted wisely with the other sons, giving them gifts rather than leaving them empty-handed. He handled his affairs with foresight and fairness, avoiding future conflict.

This gently reminds us to steward what God has entrusted to us with wisdom and care — thinking ahead, being fair, and remembering that our truest inheritance is not silver or land, but a place in God's family through Christ. What we leave behind matters, but who we belong to matters most.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I stewarding what God has given me with wisdom and fairness?
2. Do I treasure my inheritance in Christ above earthly things?
3. What kind of legacy am I preparing to leave?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in Christ I am made an heir of Your promises. Help me to steward what You have given wisely and to treasure my place in Your family most of all. Amen.
